svg.title: The analytical assurance service
svg.desc: One piece of analysis from scoping to review, drawn with the commissioner as the customer of the service. Everything below the line of visibility happens for them and not in front of them.

div.span: One piece of analysis from scoping to review, drawn with the commissioner as the customer of the service. Everything below the line of visibility happens for them and not in front of them.
What exists at the end of the stage

div.div: Scope and specification. Assurance level decision sheet. A register entry, where the work is Business Critical.
The approved design and plan, with the critical friend named on it. The quality assurance checklist for the level.
The quality assurance log: what was checked, when, and what was found. The decision log.
The output, and the quality assurance statement. Published together at Level 3.
The review record and the lessons. A revalidated designation, for Level 3 and Level 4.

div.span: The role the service is for

div.div: State the decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. Score the six impact dimensions with the analyst. Find the time the level needs, or narrow the question.
Approve the design before work proceeds, confirming it meets your need.
Stay available. Review any change of design or method. Resist changing the question late.
Confirm it meets your need, apply its limitations, and approve the results for release.
Above Level 1 the review is yours to own: with the analyst at Level 2, and with the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer at Level 3 and Level 4.

div.span: Above it, what the commissioner does. Below it, what is done for them

div.div: Clarify the real question and challenge a request that arrives framed as an output. Document the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions.
Choose the method and place it among the eight model types. Name the reviewer before the work starts.
Do the work. Your own verification and validation first. Quantify the uncertainty and log decisions as you go.
Write it up with the caveats in the output itself. Produce the quality assurance statement the level requires.
Record the lessons where the next analyst will look for them.

div.span: Below it, work the commissioner does not watch happen
Independent advice on this one assignment

div.div: Understand the brief, the context and how critical the work is. You are named at design, not found at delivery.
Review the plan. Confirm the approach answers the question and the assurance planned is at the right level. Put your own time in the schedule.
Run the checks for the level. Reproduce the calculations from source at Level 2 and above. Report errors and improvements back.
Communicate the assurance state: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented.
What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids.
Named at scoping. Confirm the Business Critical status, the register entry, and that resources and plans are in place.
Confirm design governance has been followed before the analysis starts.
Stay aware of progress, and be available to approve at delivery.
Review the assurance evidence, then approve as fit for its intended use. At Level 4 the Lead Assurer signs off first, then you.
Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose.

div.span: Below it, roles that stand behind every piece of work rather than this one
Who holds them is in the governance and management framework, not in this playbook

div.div: The Analytical Quality and Assurance Lead confirms levels and takes a level dispute. The Business Critical register holds the entry.
The governance and management framework names who holds each role, so a change of post holder is not a change to the guidance.
Information governance, before the work starts, where personal data is involved.
The Head of Profession for Statistics is the route for whether an output is fit to publish.
The senior officer accountable for analysis answers for the activity, not for any one output.

Any one impact
dimension at 4?

Settled here, at scoping, by the commissioner and the analyst together. Yes makes the work Business Critical: Level 4, a register entry, and a named Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, all from this stage. No leaves the level the matrix gave it. Everything else on this blueprint applies either way.

div.span: The three lines are the notation. The line of interaction separates what the commissioner does from what is done for them. The line of visibility separates work they see from work they do not. The line of internal interaction separates this piece of work from the roles that stand behind all of it.
NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Kainos Software Limited, SOW-DOC053.
